lessons.title: Regulatory structure
lessons.objective: Distinguish EU rules, national implementation and EASA guidance.
lessons.content: Regulation 2019/947 governs UAS operations and pilot competence; 2019/945 governs product requirements and classes. EASA publishes AMC and GM. National authorities implement rules and publish local constraints. Check the current legal text before relying on training material.

lessons.title: Open category and classes
lessons.objective: Differentiate A1, A2 and A3 and identify applicable aircraft class and pilot competence.
lessons.content: Open operations are low risk and subject to conditions including visual line of sight, height limits and restrictions on people. A1, A2 and A3 have different limitations. Class marking, mass and intended operation determine the applicable conditions. A1/A3 training is not a blanket permission to fly any drone anywhere.

lessons.title: Responsibilities and reporting
lessons.objective: Distinguish operator and remote pilot responsibilities, registration and reporting.
lessons.content: The operator manages compliance and registration where required. The remote pilot must be competent for the intended operation and comply with relevant limitations. Establish which occurrence reporting obligations apply; record and report safety events through the appropriate channels.

lessons.title: Safety decisions
lessons.objective: Recognise unsafe conditions, unsafe conduct and the need to stop.
lessons.content: The pilot should consider the aircraft, environment and personal readiness before operating. If safety cannot be maintained, do not start or discontinue the operation safely. Do not transport dangerous goods under the Open category.

lessons.title: People and other aircraft
lessons.objective: Recognise uninvolved people, assemblies, and the duty to avoid collision.
lessons.content: Keep the operation within applicable limits around people and property. Open operations must not fly over assemblies of people. Give way to other aircraft; do not continue if the operation creates a risk to other airspace users.

lessons.title: Visual observation
lessons.objective: Explain VLOS, observation and awareness of the surrounding area.
lessons.content: Visual line of sight requires continuous unaided visual contact sufficient to control the aircraft relative to people, obstacles and other aircraft. An observer may assist under applicable conditions, but the remote pilot remains responsible. Explain relevant risks to involved participants.

lessons.title: Geographical zones
lessons.objective: Identify the purpose of UAS geographical zones and their conditions.
lessons.content: Member States may restrict, prohibit or facilitate UAS operations in defined areas. A zone may specify additional conditions or an authorization requirement. An Open category proof of completion does not remove local airspace restrictions.

lessons.title: Authoritative information
lessons.objective: Locate current information from national authorities and distinguish it from informal maps.
lessons.content: Use the official national source for current geographical zones and applicable restrictions. Check the validity and time of information; an old screenshot or commercial map alone may not be sufficient.

lessons.title: Geo-awareness
lessons.objective: Explain the limitations of geo-awareness functions.
lessons.content: Geo-awareness may alert a pilot to geographical restrictions based on loaded data. Data may be incomplete or outdated. It is an aid to awareness, not an authorization or substitute for current official information.

lessons.title: Fitness to operate
lessons.objective: Recognise effects of fatigue, illness, substances and medication.
lessons.content: Fatigue, alcohol, illness and certain medicines may impair attention, reaction time and judgement. Do not operate when unfit. Seek appropriate medical advice where necessary.

lessons.title: Perception and workload
lessons.objective: Recognise limits in distance, height, speed and orientation estimation.
lessons.content: Small aircraft can be difficult to see, and visual cues vary with lighting, contrast and distance. High workload can reduce the ability to detect hazards. Keep tasks manageable and avoid distractions.

lessons.title: Situational awareness
lessons.objective: Explain how environmental conditions affect awareness, including at night.
lessons.content: Maintain an accurate understanding of the aircraft, environment and other airspace users. Reduced lighting and glare can make hazards harder to perceive. Apply applicable night-operation conditions and stop if safe awareness cannot be maintained.

lessons.title: Pre-operation planning
lessons.objective: Identify the need to assess weather, site, equipment and persons before a civilian flight.
lessons.content: Review applicable restrictions, weather and the manufacturer instructions before deciding whether the intended civilian operation is safe. Consider obstacles, uninvolved people, equipment condition and the suitability of the area.

lessons.title: Normal and abnormal situations
lessons.objective: Distinguish normal, contingency and emergency procedures in approved instructions.
lessons.content: The manufacturer instructions and applicable operator procedures define how to manage abnormal events. Understand when the operation must be discontinued and when to seek help. Prioritise safety of people and other aircraft over completing the task.

lessons.title: Post-operation records
lessons.objective: Explain the purpose of defect reporting, maintenance and flight records.
lessons.content: Record relevant activity and defects as required. Do not return defective equipment to service without appropriate action. Follow the applicable maintenance and occurrence reporting requirements.

lessons.title: Aircraft and basic flight
lessons.objective: Identify major aircraft components and factors affecting flight.
lessons.content: A UAS includes the unmanned aircraft and the equipment needed to control it remotely. Aircraft designs differ. Mass, wind, temperature and energy reserves can affect performance. Use the manufacturer limitations for the specific civilian aircraft.

lessons.title: Control and automation
lessons.objective: Explain the role and limitations of command and control and automatic functions.
lessons.content: A command-and-control link supports communication between the remote pilot station and aircraft. Automation does not remove pilot responsibility. Familiarisation with the user manual is necessary to understand limitations, alerts and safe use.

lessons.title: Equipment care
lessons.objective: Recognise battery, rotor and maintenance hazards and the purpose of technical features.
lessons.content: Rotating parts and damaged batteries can cause injury. Follow manufacturer guidance on handling, charging, storage and maintenance. Remote identification and geo-awareness have distinct purposes; neither replaces regulatory compliance.

lessons.title: Privacy risks
lessons.objective: Recognise when images or other data can affect personal privacy.
lessons.content: Drone sensors can capture identifiable people, locations and other sensitive information. Consider whether collection is necessary and lawful; avoid unnecessary collection.

lessons.title: Data protection principles
lessons.objective: Identify core GDPR principles and distinguish them from aviation authorization.
lessons.content: Where GDPR applies, personal data processing must have a lawful basis and comply with purpose limitation, minimisation, accuracy, retention and security principles. Permission to fly is not automatically permission to collect personal data.

lessons.title: Responsible records
lessons.objective: Explain access, retention and disclosure responsibilities.
lessons.content: Restrict access to personal information and retain it only as justified. Follow organisational procedures and applicable law for disclosure, deletion and rights requests.

lessons.title: Liability
lessons.objective: Explain the difference between legal liability and insurance.
lessons.content: An operator may be liable for damage arising from an operation. Insurance may cover specified risks, subject to policy terms. Liability does not disappear simply because an aircraft is insured.

lessons.title: Applicable requirements
lessons.objective: Recognise EU and national insurance requirements may vary.
lessons.content: Insurance requirements depend on the operation, applicable legislation and jurisdiction. Confirm current requirements with the relevant authority or qualified insurer rather than assuming the same rules apply everywhere.

lessons.title: Coverage verification
lessons.objective: Identify why coverage and exclusions need review.
lessons.content: Before operation, verify that any required insurance is valid and appropriate for the intended activity. Check policy dates, scope and exclusions. Keep evidence where required.

lessons.title: Safety and security
lessons.objective: Distinguish accidental safety hazards from deliberate interference or misuse.
lessons.content: Safety focuses on accidental harm; security addresses intentional threats and misuse. Both can overlap. Report security concerns through authorised channels and follow applicable procedures.

lessons.title: Information protection
lessons.objective: Recognise the need to protect accounts, records and equipment access.
lessons.content: Use authorised accounts, protect credentials, limit access to those with a legitimate need and report suspected compromise. Do not upload protected information to unapproved services.

lessons.title: National requirements
lessons.objective: Recognise that security restrictions can differ between jurisdictions.
lessons.content: National security rules may impose additional conditions on civilian UAS activities, including access to certain areas or data. Verify local requirements and obtain any necessary permissions before operating.

questions.prompt: Which EU regulation primarily governs UAS operations?
questions.explanation: 2019/947. Review Regulatory structure.

questions.prompt: What does 2019/945 principally address?
questions.explanation: UAS product requirements and classes. Review Regulatory structure.

questions.prompt: Does A1/A3 proof authorize every Open operation?
options: No, applicable aircraft and operational conditions still apply
questions.explanation: No, applicable aircraft and operational conditions still apply. Review Open category and classes.

questions.prompt: Who must comply with the operational limitations during a flight?
questions.explanation: The remote pilot. Review Responsibilities and reporting.

questions.prompt: What should an operator do about applicable occurrence reporting?
questions.explanation: Use the required reporting channels. Review Responsibilities and reporting.

questions.prompt: Which document provides acceptable means of compliance and guidance?
questions.explanation: EASA AMC and GM. Review Regulatory structure.

questions.prompt: What if safety cannot be maintained before a flight?
questions.explanation: Do not commence. Review Safety decisions.

questions.prompt: May Open category operations fly over assemblies of people?
questions.explanation: No. Review People and other aircraft.

questions.prompt: Who has priority when other aircraft create a conflict?
options: Other aircraft must be given way to
questions.explanation: Other aircraft must be given way to. Review People and other aircraft.

questions.prompt: What does VLOS require?
questions.explanation: Adequate continuous unaided visual contact. Review Visual observation.

questions.prompt: Does an observer remove the remote pilot’s responsibilities?
questions.explanation: No. Review Visual observation.

questions.prompt: What can a geographical zone impose?
questions.explanation: Additional restrictions or conditions. Review Geographical zones.

questions.prompt: Which source should be checked for current restrictions?
questions.explanation: The official national source. Review Authoritative information.

questions.prompt: Does a geo-awareness alert grant authorization?
options: Only if the battery is full
questions.explanation: No. Review Geo-awareness.

questions.prompt: Can a valid A1/A3 proof override a prohibited zone?
options: Only if the pilot is experienced
questions.explanation: No. Review Geographical zones.

questions.prompt: How can fatigue affect performance?
options: It can impair attention and judgement
questions.explanation: It can impair attention and judgement. Review Fitness to operate.

questions.prompt: What should an unfit pilot do?
questions.explanation: Not operate. Review Fitness to operate.

questions.prompt: Why can distance estimation be difficult?
options: Lighting, contrast and size affect visual cues
questions.explanation: Lighting, contrast and size affect visual cues. Review Perception and workload.

questions.prompt: What can reduced lighting affect?
questions.explanation: Detection of hazards. Review Situational awareness.

questions.prompt: Which information belongs in a pre-operation review?
options: Weather, restrictions, site and equipment condition
Only the price of the drone
questions.explanation: Weather, restrictions, site and equipment condition. Review Pre-operation planning.

questions.prompt: What should guide handling of abnormal situations?
questions.explanation: Applicable procedures and manufacturer instructions. Review Normal and abnormal situations.

questions.prompt: What takes priority over completing a task?
options: Safety of people and other aircraft
questions.explanation: Safety of people and other aircraft. Review Normal and abnormal situations.

questions.prompt: What should happen to a significant equipment defect?
options: Record it and follow appropriate corrective procedures
Ignore it if the aircraft looks new
questions.explanation: Record it and follow appropriate corrective procedures. Review Post-operation records.

questions.prompt: What is a purpose of flight records?
questions.explanation: Traceability and safety monitoring. Review Post-operation records.

questions.prompt: Is the weather alone sufficient for deciding to fly?
options: No, other relevant conditions must also be considered
questions.explanation: No, other relevant conditions must also be considered. Review Pre-operation planning.

questions.prompt: What can affect aircraft performance?
questions.explanation: Mass and environmental conditions. Review Aircraft and basic flight.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a C2 link?
options: Communication for control of the unmanned aircraft
questions.explanation: Communication for control of the unmanned aircraft. Review Control and automation.

questions.prompt: Does automation remove pilot responsibility?
questions.explanation: No. Review Control and automation.

questions.prompt: What should guide battery handling?
questions.explanation: Manufacturer safety instructions. Review Equipment care.

questions.prompt: What is the correct approach to technical safety features?
questions.explanation: Understand their functions and limitations. Review Equipment care.

questions.prompt: Can imagery of identifiable people involve personal data?
questions.explanation: Yes. Review Privacy risks.

questions.prompt: Which is a GDPR principle?
questions.explanation: Data minimisation. Review Data protection principles.

questions.prompt: Does permission to fly automatically permit personal data collection?
options: Only if the camera is small
Only if the drone is new
questions.explanation: No. Review Data protection principles.

questions.prompt: How should personal records be handled?
options: Limit access and retention as justified
questions.explanation: Limit access and retention as justified. Review Responsible records.

questions.prompt: Does insurance eliminate legal liability?
questions.explanation: No. Review Liability.

questions.prompt: Can insurance requirements vary by jurisdiction?
questions.explanation: Yes. Review Applicable requirements.

questions.prompt: What should be checked in an insurance policy?
questions.explanation: Validity, scope and exclusions. Review Coverage verification.

questions.prompt: What is a security concern?
questions.explanation: Deliberate unauthorized interference or misuse. Review Safety and security.

questions.prompt: How should protected information be handled?
options: Use approved services and authorised access
questions.explanation: Use approved services and authorised access. Review Information protection.

questions.prompt: Can national security rules add conditions to civilian UAS activities?
options: Only if a camera is absent
questions.explanation: Yes. Review National requirements.
